claims.text: A WNbMoTaV refractory high-entropy-alloy coating laser-clad onto TC4 will increase surface hardness and wear resistance relative to bare TC4.
Approximately 3.5 kW is the optimized laser power for producing the proposed coating.
The feedstock consists of equimolar, 99.5%-pure W, Mo, Ta, Nb, and V powders mechanically alloyed and granulated into spherical particles.
The intervention deposits a 2 mm-thick WNbMoTaV coating using a 5 mm laser spot, 600 mm/min scan speed, 20 mm defocus, and helium shielding at 15 L/min.
The coating will form a dense layer metallurgically bonded to the TC4 substrate.
The coating microstructure will primarily comprise a refined, high-strength BCC solid solution.
A minor Ti-rich phase will form because of rapid solidification and interaction with the substrate.
Processing near 3.5 kW minimizes unfused powder and substrate dilution.
Lattice distortion in the BCC solid solution produces solid-solution strengthening.
The refined microstructure produces grain-boundary strengthening.
Fine grains limit plastic deformation and plowing during sliding wear.
A protective tribo-oxide layer forms during sliding and further reduces wear.
Bare TC4 has an average hardness of approximately 341.25 HV0.3 under the stated baseline conditions.
Bare TC4 has a wear-volume loss of approximately 6.09×10^7 μm^3 under the stated reciprocating-sliding conditions.
The 3.5 kW coating will have hardness above 341.25 HV0.3 and wear-volume loss below 6.09×10^7 μm^3.
Hardness and wear performance depend nonmonotonically on laser power, with an optimum near 3.5 kW.
Coatings produced at 3.1 or 3.9 kW have shown poorer quality than coatings produced near 3.5 kW.
The predicted improvement applies during reciprocating sliding against a 4 mm Si3N4 ball at 20 N, a 2 mm track, 1 Hz, and 30 minutes.

contradictions.description: The hardness load is internally inconsistent: HV0.3 denotes a nominal 0.3 kgf load (about 2.94 N), whereas the stated 0.98 N load corresponds to HV0.1. Consequently, the proposed test may not be identical to the test used for the 341.25 HV0.3 baseline.
